artifact: Numerical research and independent fixtures; no product edits

referenceEnvironment.note: Reference packages are isolated outside product checkout.

priorityFixes: Introduce direct normalSf, gammaQ, beta complementary-tail, StudentSf, and FSf APIs. Never compute a very small upper tail by subtracting a rounded CDF from 1.
Every series/continued fraction must report convergence. Exceeding an iteration cap must trigger a vetted fallback or explicit unsupported-range error; never return a partial sum as a probability.
Fix Student central argument cancellation independently of degree limits. Compute t*t/(df+t*t) directly near t=0, rather than 1-df/(df+t*t).
Replace fixed inverse quantile brackets with adaptive positive bracketing and inversion of the smaller direct tail. Permit heavy-tail quantiles beyond +/-1e6.

Require finite, strictly positive shape/df inputs, deliberate support endpoints, and finite computed outputs. Validate internal regularized-beta x in [0,1]; do not turn invalid inputs into ordinary 0/1 outputs.
Large shape/df support requires stable log-normalization and asymptotic regimes, not only more loop iterations. An explicit limited numerical range is preferable to an undetected inaccurate result.

normal.method: Central normal-integral power series for 0<=z<2; backward Laplace continued fraction for z>=2, then symmetry.
normal.formula: SF(z)=phi(z)/(z+1/(z+2/(z+3/(...)))) for z>0. Central mass integral equals sum[n>=0] (-1)^n*z^(2n+1)/(2^n*n!*(2n+1)*sqrt(2*pi)).
normal.accuracyQualification: Observed numerical errors are grid measurements, not a proof of a uniform error bound. The reference treats each JavaScript binary64 input exactly. Use relative tolerance 1e-12 plus a few smallest subnormal units for SF; use absolute 2e-12 for logSF.
usage: CDF(x)=SF(-x) for x<=0; CDF(x)=1-SF(x) for x>0. CDF rounding to exactly 1 at large positive x is expected; the separately computed SF must remain nonzero while representable.
Two-sided normal p=2*SF(abs(z)); do not form 2*(1-CDF(abs(z))).
For inverse upper tail pass q directly; constructing p=1-q destroys small q. Invert logSF for subnormal q.
For positive-tail intervals a<b, use SF(a)-SF(b), or exp(logSF(a)) * -expm1(logSF(b)-logSF(a)) for narrow intervals. Avoid CDF(b)-CDF(a) in the far positive tail.
normalSf(40) underflows to zero in binary64; normalLogSf(40) remains meaningful. Clearly distinguish underflow from an exact zero probability.

shapeLimits.answer: There is no universally reliable maximum df for the existing implementation: accuracy depends on both degrees/shape and the evaluation point, with independent cancellation failures even at df=100. A shape limit is an interim scope restriction, not a numerical proof.

interimRecommendation.requirements: Apply only after direct-tail, Student-center, convergence, and input fixes; retain lower positive-shape tests. Beyond this range show unsupported precision or use a vetted large-parameter algorithm. These values target ~1e-10 relative accuracy on tested ordinary cases, not all possible inputs.

shapeLimits.gridDefinition: Gamma: selected a from .5 through 1e8, x=a+k*sqrt(a), k in {-8,-4,-2,0,1,2,4,8}, positive x only, plus special cases. Beta: a,b selected from {.5,1,2,10,100,1000,5000,10000,1e5,1e6,1e8,1e12}, x around mean by {-4,-2,0,2,4} standard deviations, selected combinations. Exact case lists in current-numerical-probe.json.
shapeLimits.largeParameterRecommendation: Use a tested incomplete-gamma implementation with Temme large-a expansion and an incomplete-beta implementation with balanced/unbalanced shape regimes, e.g. the algorithm families documented by Boost. Porting library code requires preserving its actual license. A simple normal approximation or a first asymptotic term is not an exact substitute; label approximation and verify error over an explicit supported domain.
shapeLimits.largeGammaStructure: lambda=x/a; eta=sign(lambda-1)*sqrt(2*(lambda-1-log(lambda))); Q(a,x)=normalSf(eta*sqrt(a))+S(a,eta), where S is the correction expansion. Omitting S leaves an O(1/sqrt(a)) center error: at a=1e6,x=a, Q is .4998670192391274 rather than .5.

directTailTransformations.gamma: Current x>=a+1 continued-fraction branch already computes Q as factor*h. Return it directly for gammaQ and form P only when needed. In x<a+1 branch the positive series computes P directly. Return {p,q,logp,logq,converged,iterations} where feasible; choose the direct expression for the smaller tail. Clamping cannot repair nonconvergence.
directTailTransformations.beta: I_x(a,b) complements I_(1-x)(b,a), but a small complementary argument must be formed directly from the original statistic, not as 1-x after x has rounded to 1. Expose a beta-tail API accepting both accurately computed x and y=1-x, or a dedicated transformed-distribution SF. Computing betaQ by 1-betaP is insufficient.
directTailTransformations.student: For t>=0, r=t/sqrt(df). If r<=1, u=r*r/(1+r*r) is an accurate central argument; central mass=.5*I_u(.5,df/2), giving CDF=.5+mass and SF=.5-mass when this remains well-conditioned. For tails use SF=.5*I_v(df/2,.5), with v=1/(1+r*r) for r<=1, or v=s*s/(1+s*s), s=sqrt(df)/t, for r>1 to avoid r*r overflow. Select the tail form before subtractive cancellation becomes severe, e.g. use central form only while its beta value is <=.5. Negative t uses symmetry. Preserve log(v) if v itself underflows but the beta tail remains representable (very small df can cause this).
directTailTransformations.studentCenterVerified: Replacing the current center formula by .5+.5*I_u(.5,df/2) gives .5000003979461869 (df100), .5000003988425573 (df1000), .500000398932307 (df10000), and .500000398941283 (df100000), each at t=1e-6 and consistent with independent references.
directTailTransformations.f: For x>0, compute u=df1*x/(df1*x+df2), v=df2/(df1*x+df2) through stable ratios. CDF=I_u(df1/2,df2/2), SF=I_v(df2/2,df1/2). If R=(df1/df2)*x overflows, use its reciprocal via (df2/df1)/x, avoiding infinity/infinity. In an explicitly bounded df range this handles very large x; for arbitrary finite dfs use logarithmic ratios.
directTailTransformations.inverseStudent: Use symmetry to invert q=min(p,1-p) as a positive-tail probability, bracket [0,hi] with hi doubled until SF(hi)<=q, then safeguarded bisection/Newton. Expose inverse survival for direct tiny q. Stop on bracket-width and probability criteria; signal overflow/nonconvergence rather than clipping.

additionalRegressionProperties: normalCdf(x)=normalSf(-x); normalSf is nonincreasing and in [0,1].
Exact symmetry: I_.5(a,a)=.5; Student CDF(0,df)=.5; F CDF(1,df,df)=.5.
Check direct tails in relative error; an absolute 1e-8 tolerance would incorrectly let every tiny-tail test pass with zero.
Exercise both sides of the normal z=2 algorithm boundary and gamma x=a+1 branch boundary.
Use gamma P+Q=1 and beta P+Q=1 as supporting checks, not accuracy proof: two wrong complementary numbers still sum to 1.
Quantile round trips must use independent reference values and the same smaller tail; testing only implementation against itself can miss shared bugs.
Validation: NaN/Infinity degrees, nonpositive df, invalid probabilities, negative shape, and out-of-domain regularized-beta x must not produce a plausible numeric result.

sources.supports: Error-function power series, equation 7.6.1; rescale argument to z/sqrt(2).
Laplace continued fraction for the complementary error function, equation 7.9.1; equivalent to the normal Mills-ratio fraction.
Regularized incomplete beta, symmetry, and continued fractions.
Uniform large-parameter incomplete-gamma expansion. Requires correction terms and stable treatment near x=a.
Different large-parameter incomplete-beta asymptotics for balanced and unbalanced shapes.
Direct regularized upper incomplete gamma and independent fixture implementation.
Direct complementary regularized incomplete beta and independent fixture implementation.
Vetted algorithm selection and accuracy discussion for incomplete gamma.
Vetted incomplete-beta implementation uses several regimes; points to DiDonato and Morris algorithms.
Student t density, df=1 Cauchy special case, normal limit.
F CDF expressed as one minus incomplete beta with complementary argument.
